The Boundary Chart

Mathematics in James boundary arithmetic, one law per step, from the void toward F₁. Every law is drawn, glossed, derived from the laws before it, and checked by the engine. Built so far: rungs void, N, Z, mult, Q, alg and C — through the named forms and the J-discipline of James 1993, Chapters 3–5 (the Pythagorean identity, ω² + ω + 1, the conjugate and the angle-addition formulas are owed).

The void

≐

Zero is what you have when you have written nothing at all; adding nothing changes nothing.

classical holdsJ1 holdsJH holdsJO holdsJP holdsC EXACTfinset EXACTlambda untestedCC untestedlogic EXACT

none — adjoined. This is a fact of the medium, not an axiom: "A void" and "A" are the same inscription.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The additive identity 0, and the fact that it is unique: there is only one way to write nothing. It is not yet the number zero as an object you can point at — that arrives as a value, (□) ≐ void, at mult.hole-instance. In Laws of Form this is the unmarked state.

void.spaceprimitiveNATIVEengineshape-ledband Kmedium●

Space — juxtaposition is unordered

≐
A B ≐ B AA B ≐ A Ba + b = b + a

Things sitting together on a page have no first or second; so adding is the same in either order, for free.

classical holdsJ1 holdsJH holdsJO holdsJP holdsC EXACTfinset EXACTlambda untestedCC untestedlogic EXACT
Derivation

none — adjoined. A fact of the medium; its unit is the void, void.page.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

The additive layer of arithmetic is a commutative monoid with the void as unit — before any number has been written. It is not multiplication: juxtaposition becomes multiplication only under an instance boundary, ([A][B]), at mult.multiplication. And it is the deepest design decision in the calculus: because breadth is unordered, no non-commutative product can ever live in it (the No-Go theorem, JH-1 — a later node).

Confirms

The natural numbers as unary numerals: every n ≥ 1 is a pile, and 0 is the void (void.page). This is not positional notation — the calculus has no base — and it is not Laws of Form: there o o ≐ o (the law of Calling), so LoF has no natural numbers. James's refusal of Calling is where number begins.

Confirms

0 is the additive identity. Note what it is not: zero has no inscription, so "0" cannot be pointed at as a form until the black hole gives it one — (□) ≐ void at mult.hole-instance — and it cannot be negated as a form until Z.void-inverse. The number zero has three faces in the chart: nothing, the instance of the hole, and the mirror of nothing.

This node deliberately claims only what the fragment proves.

Refuted readings

  • "nothing added later ever collapses two piles" follows from soundness in ℂ — the first draft (2026-10-03) made this claim here with an engine badge; the referee pass the same day showed the unrestricted laws do collapse the calculus unless the undefined forms are excluded, and that nothing in the engine checks a meta claim. Moved to mult.consistency, with its decree and import made explicit.

Notes

The witness tools/models/freeness_check.py enumerates piles up to twelve units and confirms their canonical forms are pairwise distinct — all that a fragment with no rewrite rules can be asked to show.

The JP cell is the first place the chart shows the place calculus doing something to ℕ rather than with it: the void pile p^N ≐ void is a decree that breaks this theorem on purpose. That is a feature of the chart, not a bug of either calculus.

Induction on a pile

GAP — 'a law that holds of void and is preserved by adjoining o holds of every pile' is not a form and not an equation
P(0) ∧ (∀n. P(n) ⇒ P(n+1)) ⇒ ∀n. P(n)

The calculus can show something for 2, for 3, for 4 — one pile at a time — but it has no way to say "and so on, forever."

classical failsJ1 failsJH failsJO failsJP failsC ABSENTfinset PARTIALlambda untestedCC untestedlogic ABSENT
Derivation

none — gap.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

That James's calculus is an equational theory of forms, not a logic: it has no quantifiers, no implication, no variables ranging over properties. Every "for all n" in the chart (every kind: schema node) is a meta-statement the reader supplies. The two ends of the chart both need this gap closed: the Lean expansion (where Nat.rec is native) and the F₁ end (where ℕ must be recognized as the free commutative monoid on o).

Confirms

That order is meta in James's calculus: it is read off normal forms, exactly as it is read off tallies. The chart's own equality field is this axiom's shadow: ≐ classical, ≡/≃ in J1 where the unit is weakened.

The depth-1 criterion (J1). A Λ-sensitive step — the unit [(X)] ≐ X in either direction, or [o] ≐ void — that sits at depth 1 under an instance boundary, passing only through angle boundaries on the way (which carry −λ ∈ Λ), is absorbed by that instance (A5′: (λ A) ≐ (A) for λ ∈ Λ), so a law whose Λ-steps are all of that kind holds exactly in J1 even though each step holds only mod Λ. The slogan "both sides under an instance" is neither necessary nor sufficient: Q.fractional-cardinality has a bare A on one side and is exact (its last step is the strict counit), while ([ [(X)] Y ]) ≐ ([X Y]) has both sides under an instance and fails (the Λ-step sits at depth 2, under a square). The Q-rung J1 cells cite this note.

That is why absorption is an axiom of semirings — it does not follow from the other semiring laws — and a theorem of rings; the chart's price ledger shows the same fact as a cost.

Dominion is independent of Involution and Distribution

□ A ≐ □ is not derivable from Involution + Distribution; it is derivable once Inversion is adjoined
a semiring need not have an absorbing zero; a ring must

Without the mirror, the page cannot prove that the bottomless pit swallows everything; here is a tiny toy world where it doesn't.

classical holdsJ1 untestedJH untestedJO untestedJP holdsC EXACTfinset untestedlambda untestedCC untestedlogic untested
Derivation
statementrulenote
A model of the medium plus Involution and Distribution is a commutative monoid (M, +, 0) — the multiset syntax forces commutativity and associativity — with a bijection e : M → M (the round boundary), l = e⁻¹ (the square), satisfying e(a + l(b + c)) = e(a + l b) + e(a + l c) for all a, b, c; the angle boundary may be interpreted by any map, since no axiom of this fragment constrains itvoid.space mult.involution mult.distributionany equational derivation is sound in any such total algebra
Take M = {0, 1, 2} with 0 the unit, 1 + 1 = 1, 1 + 2 = 1, 2 + 2 = 2; e(0) = 2, e(1) = 1, e(2) = 0—the witness; tools/models/dominion_models.py checks all 27 instances of Distribution
In this model □ = l(0) = 2 ≠ 0 = void, and (□) = e(2) = 0 = void as mult.hole-instance requires — but □ + 1 = 2 + 1 = 1 ≠ 2, so □ A ≐ □ fails at A = 1—hence mult.dominion is not derivable from the two axioms
M is not a group (1 has no inverse), so Z.inversion has no interpretation here — consistent with the derivation of mult.zero-annihilates and mult.dominion through Inversion—the other two axioms do not suffice; with Inversion (by those nodes) they do

The script also reports the census of labelled structures (not isomorphism classes): of all commutative monoids of order ≤ 4 with a bijection satisfying Distribution, Dominion fails in 1 of 2 (order 2), 4 of 8 (order 3), 42 of 78 (order 4); those counts include degenerate models with □ = void, and only the chosen witness insists on □ ≠ void. (□) ≐ void holds in every model, as it must — it is Involution at 0 (mult.hole-instance).

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

That James's three axioms are not redundant for this theorem: the additive-inverse axiom is what makes zero absorbing, exactly as in algebra at large — absorption (0·a = 0) must be postulated in a semiring because it does not follow from distributivity and the monoid laws, and is derived in a ring. The witness model is itself such a structure: a commutative pre-semiring with unit e(0) = 2 in which 0·1 = 1. The shape of the fact is textbook; what this node adds is the James-specific witness, with the exp/log bijection in place, showing where in the chart the cost falls.

The two undefined forms

You may not mirror the bottomless pit, and you may not ask what you would have to circle to get it. Both questions have no answer, and the page refuses them rather than answering wrongly.

classical holdsJ1 holdsJH holdsJO holdsJP holdsC EXACTfinset ABSENTlambda untestedCC untestedlogic untested
Derivation

none — adjoined, as a decree about the two forms built from Z.angle, mult.square and mult.black-hole. The calculus does not derive the exclusion; it legislates it, and the legislation is load-bearing. If <□> were admitted, Dominion and Inversion would give A ≐ A □ <□> ≐ □ <□> ≐ void for every A. If [□] were admitted, write W for (o [□]): Dominion inside the square gives (o [□]) ≐ (o [□ C]), Distribution gives (o [□ C]) ≐ (o [□]) (o [C]), so W ≐ W X with X = (o [C]); adjoining <W> and cancelling gives X ≐ void, i.e. (o [C]) ≐ void for every C, and with C = (<o>) the unit itself is void. Either admission makes every form equal to every other.

Division by zero as the exclusion of arithmetic, and ln(−∞) beside it. The JH extension found the same decree bans a third thing: inverting a singular matrix (JH-20: a biquaternion with norm form void demands <□>). What the decree protects is the consistency of the whole calculus (mult.consistency): the engine enforces it by raising Excluded and Undefined whenever a derivation row evaluates to one of the two forms, which is the up-to-value version of the rule.

The seam discipline

DISCIPLINE — a unit step, in either orientation ([(X)] → X or X → [(X)]), is admissible only when X lies on the principal strip in the ℂ reading (−π < Im X ≤ π), or when the redex is in an absorbing position: directly inside an instance boundary, through angle boundaries at most

The box may undo the circle only where no hidden turn has crept in, or right inside another circle, which forgets whole turns — and the page cannot itself see the hidden turn; it has to be told.

Confirms

James's own repair of the "crack" in his calculus (Chapter 5): J-cancellation permitted only inside an instance boundary, and only after other reductions. The chart states a stronger rule one rung earlier, and semantically — James's two J-rules sit inside it as special cases (C.james-discipline) — because the collapse can be written as soon as [<o>] or [[[oo]]] can — at rung mult, before J is a named form — and because no syntactic signature of "off the strip" is available in the calculus (the witness [[[oo]]] refutes the natural one). Soundness under the decree is the theorem mult.consistency. JH's seam guard — [(A)] → A only when L(exp V(A)) = V(A) — is the same rule; J1's answer is different in kind: it does not refuse the step, it prices it with a receipt, and the depth-1 criterion (mult.involution, Notes) says when the price is absorbed.

Refuted readings

  • the guard need only cover the orientation [(X)] → X — the first statement of this decree (2026-10-03); refuted the same day by the alg referee pass: the collapse runs backwards through X → [(X)] (Notes).
  • the pilot's rungs need no guard on Involution-down; the J-discipline is rung C's business — refuted 2026-10-03 (second referee pass): J J = [<o>][<o>] is writable at rung mult, and the collapse above uses only rungs ≤ Q.
  • "phased" — a square with an angle somewhere inside it — is a sufficient syntactic signature for off-strip content, so the decree can be stated in forms alone — refuted the same day by the consistency witness (tools/models/consistency_check.py): [[[oo]]] = ln(ln ln 2) has imaginary part π with no angle anywhere, and [[[oo]]] [[[oo]]] is off the strip. Sign is lost under iterated squares, not only under mirrors; which iterated squares lose it depends on values ([[ooo]] is positive, [[oo]] negative). The decree is therefore semantic, and its nativity is the gap mult.seam-signature.

Notes

The collapse the decree blocks, using only laws of rungs ≤ Q. Start from o; by the unit law right to left, o ≐ ([o] [o]); by the product of negatives right to left, ≐ ([<o>] [<o>]). Abstract both sides: void ≐ [o] ≐ [([<o>] [<o>])], and one unguarded unit step, [([<o>][<o>])] → [<o>] [<o>], gives [<o>] [<o>] ≐ void — James's J-cancellation J J ≐ void, whose content is 2πi. From it: J ≐ <J> by Inversion; with H = ([J] <[oo]>) (half of J), cardinality gives H H ≐ J, and the ℚ sign rule for a mirrored numerator turns H ≐ ([H H] <[oo]>) ≐ ([<H H>] <[oo]>) into <H>; so J ≐ H H ≐ H <H> ≐ void, <o> ≐ ([<o>]) ≐ (void) ≐ o, and oo ≐ o <o> ≐ void. Every step but the marked one is exact in ℂ. The marked step is refused by this decree: its content has imaginary part 2π and its position (depth 0) is not absorbing. (An earlier Refuted entry spoke of "the collapse above"; it is this one.) Run backwards — [<o>] [<o>] → [([<o>] [<o>])] → [([o] [o])] → [o] → void — the same collapse uses the unit in the other orientation, which is why both are guarded. The same route runs, mutatis mutandis, from N = [[oo]], a negative number reached with no mirror: ([N][N]) ≐ ([<N>][<N>]) (both 0.1343), the unguarded step [([N][N])] → [N][N] (content −2.007 + 2πi), and J′ = [N] <[<N>]> (value iπ) in J's role — which is why the guard must look at values and not at mirrors (mult.seam-signature). The "ℚ sign rule for a mirrored numerator" above is Q.negative-fraction.

Price. The guard imports the ℂ reading, which overcharges: only Im X — the branch index — is needed, not the whole value (and not Im X mod 2π, which destroys exactly the information the strip test uses); a cheaper branch-reading import would price the sign laws more exactly. Laws whose unit steps are admitted by content at non-absorbing positions (alg.log-law and C.log-of-negative at depth 0; alg.root-of-product and alg.power-of-power under a square), and laws whose unit steps are seam steps admitted by position (Q.reciprocal-of-negative, C.period-absorption, C.euler-formula), declare guarded_by: [mult.seam-decree] — a field the checker computes from the derivation and enforces both ways — and so carry the guard in their price; their descendants inherit it through uses. Their status stays NATIVE: the decree adjudicates the step, it does not make the law true (Amendment A2, after the C referee pass found the two clauses priced inconsistently between rungs Q and C).

The engine enforces this decree directly (tools/check.py, check_seam): for every step that is a unit step, it evaluates the content on the node's sampled domain and refuses the step if the content leaves the strip in any sample while the position is not absorbing. Schemas are checked on their sampled instances; a law whose derivation needs an unguarded unit step for some instances must either restructure the step into an absorbing position or restrict its domain and say so.

Confirms

That James's "crack" is deeper than the phase element: it is the absence, in an equational calculus of forms, of any term for the branch of a logarithm. The classical calculus is consistent only relative to a guard it imports. This is exactly the place where the enrichment program enters: 𝕁₁ does not guard the unit, it weakens it to [(A)] ≐ A mod Λ and records that the discrepancy lies in Λ as a receipt. A receipt is bookkeeping of an unknown, not detection — the calculus never determines which λ without the reading — but it dissolves the gap wherever an instance encloses the step (A5′ absorbs every λ) and leaves it open exactly for bare abstracts, which is what the J1 cells of alg.log-law and alg.power-of-power say. Seen from below, the receipt calculus is what this gap becomes.

Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

Two cautions the argument needs. The guard covers the unit in both orientations ([(X)] ≐ X is false off the strip either way). And the admissible calculus is not substitution-closed: a derived schema such as alg.log-law is admissible only on the domain where its own derivation is — instantiated at A = B = <o> it is the collapse step — so a law may be cited only inside its declared domain; the engine re-evaluates every row, which is how it catches a bad instantiation.

James's soundness result, scoped exactly: the calculus is consistent as a calculus of admissible derivations under the J-discipline, and both devices are hinges, not afterthoughts. Once the unit is guarded, soundness is immediate — every other rule is an identity of complex arithmetic — so the whole weight of consistency rests on a guard the calculus cannot state in its own terms. It is not yet re-established for the enriched settings, each of which changes the reading and the axioms (JH-22 is the JH version: consistency relative to ℍ).

(−a)⁻¹ = −a⁻¹, by uniqueness of inverses, as in any field. What the chart adds is the price: three of the steps are the unit on content off the principal strip, admitted only because they sit inside an instance — seam steps, so the law declares guarded_by (by position) and is the first sign law to carry the decree in its price (its status stays NATIVE: the decree adjudicates the steps, it does not make the law true — Amendment A2). In J1 the same three steps post receipts of ±2πi, and the law holds exactly by the depth-1 criterion; these are the first ℚ laws whose receipts do not vanish. The engine passes every row because it evaluates whole rows: the periods cancel inside the instance.

A circle around a circle is the number e — the first number on the page that no fraction can name.

Confirms

e as e^1, the value the exponential takes at the unit. What this does not do is constrain the base: the three axioms never mention a value for (o) — read with (A) = b^A and [A] = log_b A, every object-level law of the chart holds for any base b > 0, b ≠ 1 (checked for b = 2, 10, ½ by the alg referee pass), so the calculus cannot even refute e ≐ oo: in the base-2 reading (o) and oo have the same value. Where the classical setting does commit to e is the ℂ reading it imports (mult.c-reading, (A) = e^A) and the seam decree that inherits it, whose strip (−π, π] is base e's. Whether the rules determine every true identity of exp and log is a different question, the exp–log completeness question of the analysis rung. Transcendence of e (Hermite 1873) is an import the calculus cannot state (alg.irrationality is the simpler version of the same gap).

Algebraic numbers that radicals cannot reach

GAP — no radical form reaches the real root of x⁵ − x − 1 (Abel–Ruffini); whether any form at all does is open: the forms' values are Chow's exp–log numbers, and 'no non-radical algebraic number is an exp–log number' is Chow's conjecture, a theorem only under Schanuel's conjecture (Chow 1999)
not every algebraic number is a radical expression; whether one can be an exp–log number is open

The page can write any number you can reach with roots. Some solutions of simple equations lie beyond every stack of roots; whether the page's other shapes — logs of logs, exponentials of sums — reach them is unsettled.

Confirms

That James's remark "the calculus covers the integers, the rationals, and the algebraic irrationals" is proven only for the radical irrationals; the stronger reading is refuted if Schanuel's conjecture holds (Chow 1999, Theorem 2) and survives only if Schanuel fails. A root-finding construction — an iteration that converges — would reach every real algebraic number regardless; that is the same shape as the gaps at Q.lowest-terms (Euclid) and N.induction: a process on forms, not a form.

  • Lehmer's number is a radical form — refuted 2026-10-01 in the exp–log thread: the Galois group of its degree-5 trace polynomial is S₅, so the Galois group of the degree-10 Lehmer polynomial is not solvable. (The first record here said "is a form" and "Galois group S₅" of the Lehmer polynomial itself; both corrected 2026-10-03 — the group of the degree-10 polynomial lies in C₂ ≀ S₅ and is larger than S₅.)
  • the real root of x⁵ − x − 1 is not ≐ any form — overclaimed 2026-10-03 and corrected the same day: Abel–Ruffini excludes radical forms only; the exp–log case is Chow's conjecture.

Notes

x⁵ − x − 1 is the standard example: irreducible over ℚ, discriminant 2869 = 19·151, Galois group S₅, one real root. Chow, "What is a closed-form number?", Amer. Math. Monthly 106 (1999).

Confirms

The period of exp: e^{a + 2πi} = e^a for every complex a. This is the sound content of James's "J-cancellation": the pair cancels inside an instance because the instance forgets whole turns, and the derivation says exactly where that happens — the unit step is taken in the absorbing position, which the seam decree admits unconditionally. Its content 2πi is off the strip, so the step is a seam step and the law carries the decree in its price (guarded_by, by position): a law whose statement is an exact identity of ℂ while its derivation leans on the decree, as Q.reciprocal-of-negative and C.phase-under-instance before it. It is not J J ≐ void, and it is not [A J J] ≐ [A]: under a square J J is just the summand 2πi, and ln(a + 2πi) is not ln a. In J1 this law is the completion axiom A5′ itself, (λ A) ≐ (A) for λ ∈ Λ, at λ = ω.

e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ, with θ = πt, as a theorem of the three axioms — every step exact as a row, every unit step in an absorbing position, so the law holds for every t; the first unit step is a seam step (the sine's interior is off the strip when the sine is negative), so the derivation leans on the decree's position clause and the law carries it in its price. What the derivation is: the algebra (X + 1/X)/2 + i·(X − 1/X)/(2i) = X, done in forms. What it is not: Euler's own route, which defines cos and sin by their series and proves the formula analytically — the chart has no series until rung analysis, so here cos and sin were defined from the exponential, and the formula records that the definitions are the right ones. The Pythagorean identity cos² + sin² = 1 is the natural companion and is owed (it is ([cos][cos]) ([sin][sin]) ≐ o, the product X · 1/X = 1 in disguise). At t = 1 the sine vanishes into the hole and the law reads (J) ≐ <o>, which is C.phase-value; C.euler-identity is one Inversion further.

C.james-disciplinetheoremNATIVE-BY-DECREEenginemetaneed-ledband beyond○

James's J-discipline sits inside the seam decree

James's two J-rules, as the chart records them — convert [<A>] to [A] J on sight; cancel J J only inside an instance, and last — sit inside the seam decree: rule 1 is admitted exactly on content with Im Ln A ∈ (−π, 0] and refuted elsewhere, rule 2 is period absorption, and the decree is strictly stronger than both, since it adjudicates every unit step and not only those through J
ln(−a) = ln a + iπ only for Im Ln a ∈ (−π, 0]; e^{z + 2πi} = e^z always; 2πi ≠ 0; the Involution route to J J = 0 is closed by neither J-rule

James patched the crack by giving rules for handling J. The chart patched it by giving a rule for undoing a circle with a box. The chart's patch covers James's and more — and James's first rule, taken literally, is itself cracked.

classical holdsJ1 replacedJH replacedJO replacedJP untestedC EXACTfinset ABSENTlambda untestedCC untestedlogic ABSENT
Derivation

The J-rules compared here are the chart's paraphrase of Chapter 5 (page citations owed); the comparison is against that paraphrase.

statementrulenote
Rule 1 ⊂ content clause, restricted. "Convert [<A>] to [A] J on sight" is the law C.log-of-negative, whose one step is the unit at depth 0 on content [A] J. The decree admits it exactly when Im Ln A ∈ (−π, 0] — positive A and the lower half-plane — and the equation is false by 2πi otherwise, so James's rule as stated is unsound: it fails at A = <o> and at A = [[oo]], a negative real with no mirror in sight. The chart's rule 1 is the restriction to positive A, with C.log-of-negative-below as its companion on the other sideC.log-of-negative C.log-of-negative-below mult.seam-decreewitness part (1): on wide complex sampling the conversion is exact in roughly half the samples and off by exactly 2πi in the rest, with the boundary predicted by the strip test in every sample
Rule 2 ⊂ position clause. "Cancel J J only inside an instance, and last" is C.period-absorption (A J J) ≐ (A): the unit step it hides is a seam step taken in an absorbing position, which the decree admits; the ordering clause is unnecessary once admissibility is decided by positionC.period-absorption C.double-phasewitness part (2): exact on 300 complex samples
The decree is strictly stronger. (a) It adjudicates unit steps that involve no J at all: the seam steps of Q.reciprocal-of-negative have content −ln a − iπ and 2πi, and the J-rules say nothing about them. (b) The collapse route of mult.seam-decree reaches J J ≐ void not by cancelling J J but by one Involution step [(J J)] → J J at depth 0 — a step neither J-rule, as paraphrased, forbids; the decree refuses it by content, in both orientationsmult.seam-decree Q.reciprocal-of-negativewitness part (3): the engine's own seam check refuses [(J J)] ↔ J J both ways and admits the same step directly inside an instance, through an angle too
What the J-rules leave implicit — that J and <J> differ on the page and agree under an instance — is C.phase-signC.phase-signwitness part (4)
Where the two repairs differ in kind: James's rules are syntactic ("on sight", "inside an instance") and the first is unsound for that reason — the content [A] J leaves the strip for some A without any visible sign; the decree is semantic, and that it must be is the gap mult.seam-signaturemult.seam-signature—
Confirms · settings · notes

Confirms

That the classical setting of the chart — three boundaries, three axioms, two decrees — contains the classical James algebra of the thesis: three boundaries, three axioms, J, and the J-discipline. The discipline is not a fourth axiom and not a convention about J; it is a procedural shadow of the condition under which the unit step is harmless — true on the strip, absorbed inside an instance — and J is where the condition first bites: <J> (four boundaries, value −iπ) is the smallest form whose content leaves the half-open strip, and J J the smallest whose content leaves it by a whole period. What this node does not show: that the two repairs are equivalent (they are not — the decree is strictly stronger, and rule 1 is refuted as stated); that the decree is the only repair (J1 prices the step with a receipt instead of refusing it, and JH guards one orientation semantically); or that the decree follows from the axioms (it is adjoined, in both tellings). Nor does it certify James's own text: the rules compared are the chart's paraphrase, and the thesis may restrict Involution-down as well — the page citations are owed.

Refuted readings

  • the J-discipline and the seam decree are the same rule — the first statement of this node (2026-10-03, same day); refuted by its own body in the C referee pass: the decree adjudicates non-J seam steps and the Involution route to the crack, which the J-rules do not, and rule 1 as stated is false off the lower half-plane. Struck, and the node restated as an inclusion.
  • the J-discipline is a convention about a special symbol J, separate from the axioms — it is a special case of the admissibility condition on the unit step of mult.involution, which the chart states before J is named (an interpretive thesis, recorded rather than witnessed).

The refutations of J J ≐ void and J ≐ <J> as depth-0 laws, and of the on-sight rule for every A, live at C.double-phase, C.phase-sign and C.log-of-negative respectively.

The witness tools/models/j_discipline.py tests four facts of the ℂ reading and one behaviour of the engine (check_seam, the chart's implementation of the decree); it witnesses the rows above, not a theorem about two derivation systems — that would need James's rules formalized from the text. James 1993, Chapter 5, page citations are owed (the chart's copy of the thesis is the 2026 transcription). The 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-03 sessions found the collapse route independently and legislated the decree at rung mult under referee pressure; this node closes that loop by placing James's own rules inside it.

period

2πi, as J J: the smallest form whose content leaves the principal strip by a whole turn. An instance forgets it ((A J J) ≐ (A)), a square remembers it, and the bare page must not throw it away — J J ≐ void is the crack James found and the seam decree closes.

phase

What J = [<o>] carries: a half-turn, read as iπ. Under an instance a phase is a sign ((A J) ≐ <(A)>), two of them are nothing ((A J J) ≐ (A)), and on the bare page they are kept exactly — which is the whole content of the seam decree. Fractions of J are the roots of unity; i is half of J.

trigonometry

Cosine and sine are defined from the phase — half the sum, and half the difference over i, of a turn and its reverse — and Euler's formula is then the theorem that the two halves reassemble the turn. No lengths, no triangles: the angle is a count of J, in half-turns. The Pythagorean identity and the angle-addition formulas are owed.

zero

Zero has three faces in the calculus: the void (nothing written), the instance of the black hole (□) (zero as a value), and the mirror of nothing <>. The chart keeps them as three laws because the extensions treat them differently.

Gapsconcepts without a form; each carries a plan

N.induction Induction on a pile — GAP — 'a law that holds of void and is preserved by adjoining o holds of every pile' is not a form and not an equation
N.order Order — m < n — GAP — 'oo < ooo' is not a form; order is a predicate on normal forms, not an equation
mult.seam-signature A native signature for the seam — GAP — the calculus cannot say in its own terms which contents are off the principal strip, so the seam discipline has to be stated in the ℂ reading
Q.lowest-terms Lowest terms — a canonical fraction — GAP — 'the reduced form of a fraction' is not an equation: deciding it needs a greatest common divisor, which is an iteration
alg.irrationality Irrationality — √2 is not a fraction — GAP — '(([[oo]] <[oo]>)) is not ≐ any fraction of piles' is a negative statement about all derivations, and the calculus has no form for it
alg.non-radical Algebraic numbers that radicals cannot reach — GAP — no radical form reaches the real root of x⁵ − x − 1 (Abel–Ruffini); whether any form at all does is open: the forms' values are Chow's exp–log numbers, and 'no non-radical algebraic number is an exp–log number' is Chow's conjecture, a theorem only under Schanuel's conjecture (Chow 1999)

Refuted readingskept, struck through, attached to the law they were mistaken for

N.freeness
  • "nothing added later ever collapses two piles" follows from soundness in ℂ — the first draft (2026-10-03) made this claim here with an engine badge; the referee pass the same day showed the unrestricted laws do collapse the calculus unless the undefined forms are excluded, and that nothing in the engine checks a meta claim. Moved to mult.consistency, with its decree and import made explicit.
Z.inversion
  • < > is the uniformizer at a finite place — refuted 2026-09-13: the mirror gives J at every place; the uniformizer at p = 2 is [oo] (p-adic-wall thread).
mult.involution
  • the tower [[[A]]] ≃ [[A]] stabilizes — refuted 2026-08-22 (collapse theorem: with ()-congruence it forces total transparency); stabilization relocated to the mixed closure [(−)] at depth 1.
mult.black-hole
  • □ is +∞ — Lui confirmed 2026-09-13 that □ is log 0 = −∞ when the engine labelled its valuation +∞; the sign depends on which axis (value or valuation) is meant.
mult.hole-instance
  • needs Distribution as well as Involution — the first draft (2026-10-03) derived this through a Distribution detour; the referee pass the same day pointed out it is Involution-up at A = void in one step. Price corrected.
mult.dominion
  • Dominion is a theorem of Involution and Distribution alone — refuted 2026-10-03 by the 3-element model in tools/models/dominion_models.py (mult.dominion-independence).
mult.hole-exclusion
  • [□] is merely an open form, unread but admissible — refuted 2026-10-03 (referee pass): admitting it collapses the calculus by the derivation above. It is excluded, and Bricken's reading of [[ ]] as complex infinity is a reading of an excluded form, not a law.
  • the decree bans only the literal string <□> — refuted the same day: any form ≐ □ (e.g. [J J] once J-cancellation is available at rung C) would bypass a literal ban; the decree is up to ≐.
mult.seam-decree
  • the guard need only cover the orientation [(X)] → X — the first statement of this decree (2026-10-03); refuted the same day by the alg referee pass: the collapse runs backwards through X → [(X)] (Notes).
  • the pilot's rungs need no guard on Involution-down; the J-discipline is rung C's business — refuted 2026-10-03 (second referee pass): J J = [<o>][<o>] is writable at rung mult, and the collapse above uses only rungs ≤ Q.
  • "phased" — a square with an angle somewhere inside it — is a sufficient syntactic signature for off-strip content, so the decree can be stated in forms alone — refuted the same day by the consistency witness (tools/models/consistency_check.py): [[[oo]]] = ln(ln ln 2) has imaginary part π with no angle anywhere, and [[[oo]]] [[[oo]]] is off the strip. Sign is lost under iterated squares, not only under mirrors; which iterated squares lose it depends on values ([[ooo]] is positive, [[oo]] negative). The decree is therefore semantic, and its nativity is the gap mult.seam-signature.
mult.seam-signature
  • "phased" (a square with an angle inside) is the signature — refuted 2026-10-03 by [[[oo]]]; recorded at mult.seam-decree.
mult.consistency
  • the unrestricted equational theory of the pilot's laws is consistent — refuted 2026-10-03 (first referee pass). Route A: with [□] admitted, W = (o [□]) satisfies W ≐ W (o [C]) by Dominion-under-square and Distribution, so Inversion gives (o [C]) ≐ void for every C, hence o ≐ void.
  • Route B needs rung C (a named J) — refuted the same day (second referee pass): J J = [<o>][<o>] is writable at rung mult; one unguarded unit step gives J J ≐ void, and the ℚ sign rules finish the collapse (recorded at mult.seam-decree). The first draft of this node deferred the guard to rung C; it is needed from rung mult on.
Q.negative-fraction
  • a/(−b) = −(a/b) follows "by the same promotion with the roles exchanged" — the first draft (2026-10-03) claimed this in prose; the referee pass the same day showed no instantiation of inverse promotion matches ([A] <[<B>]>). The bottom-sign law is Q.negative-denominator and needs Q.reciprocal-of-negative.
Q.rational
  • every form in which each pile occurs only as [pile] or <[pile]> directly under an instance is rational — refuted 2026-10-03 (second referee pass): (([oo])) = e² fits that description. The class must be stated as juxtapositions of (mirrored) instances of such contents.
alg.non-radical
  • Lehmer's number is a radical form — refuted 2026-10-01 in the exp–log thread: the Galois group of its degree-5 trace polynomial is S₅, so the Galois group of the degree-10 Lehmer polynomial is not solvable. (The first record here said "is a form" and "Galois group S₅" of the Lehmer polynomial itself; both corrected 2026-10-03 — the group of the degree-10 polynomial lies in C₂ ≀ S₅ and is larger than S₅.)
  • the real root of x⁵ − x − 1 is not ≐ any form — overclaimed 2026-10-03 and corrected the same day: Abel–Ruffini excludes radical forms only; the exp–log case is Chow's conjecture.
C.log-of-negative
  • [<A>] ≐ [A] J holds for every form A (the on-sight rule as a law) — refuted 2026-10-03 (alg referee pass) at A = [[oo]]; recorded at mult.seam-decree and C.james-discipline.
C.double-phase
  • J J ≐ void — James's J-cancellation stated without its instance; refuted as a depth-0 law 2026-10-03 (its content is 2πi; the collapse it causes is recorded at mult.seam-decree, its restatement in James's terms at C.james-discipline).
C.phase-sign
  • J ≐ <J> — false on the bare page (iπ ≠ −iπ); only its instance holds. Refuted 2026-10-03 as a step of the collapse route (mult.seam-decree).
C.james-discipline
  • the J-discipline and the seam decree are the same rule — the first statement of this node (2026-10-03, same day); refuted by its own body in the C referee pass: the decree adjudicates non-J seam steps and the Involution route to the crack, which the J-rules do not, and rule 1 as stated is false off the lower half-plane. Struck, and the node restated as an inclusion.
  • the J-discipline is a convention about a special symbol J, separate from the axioms — it is a special case of the admissibility condition on the unit step of mult.involution, which the chart states before J is named (an interpretive thesis, recorded rather than witnessed).

The refutations of J J ≐ void and J ≐ <J> as depth-0 laws, and of the on-sight rule for every A, live at C.double-phase, C.phase-sign and C.log-of-negative respectively.
